newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Gevaert 1996 profit rises 44 percent.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Gevaert 1996 profit rises 44 percent.

text.p: Belgian holding company Gevaert NV said on Wednesday gains from the sale of shares in German airline Lufthansa AG and French shipping company Cie Navigation Mixte helped lift 1996 net profit by 44 percent.
Net profit totalled 4.23 billion Belgian francs ($121 million).

Income from capital gains doubled to 2.06 billion francs from 1.09 billion francs, Gevaert said in a statement. Underlying current earnings from dividend and other income, excluding exceptionals, rose by 17 percent to 2.22 billion.
The company said it would pay out 1.89 billion francs in dividends, giving a net dividend per share of 55 francs, up 10 percent. More than 2.24 billion francs would go into reserves.
Gevaert said that during the year it cut its stake in Dutch insurer Aegon to about three percent from 3.2 percent and reduced its holding in German chemicals group Bayer .
New interests were acquired in French banking group Credit Local de France and German real estate company IVG Holding. Gevaert also increased its holding in Dutch paper company KNP BT to 9.5 percent.
The company conservatively estimated net asset value per share on February 17 as 3,007 francs. On the Brussels Stock Exchange the share closed down 20 francs at 2,500 ahead of the announcement.
